Playbook.name: Windows — Discovery of Internet Capabilities via Built-in Tools - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A host ran ping/tracert/pathping to a non-local target for the first time in the baseline window (new_terms) - checking internet reachability, an early step malware uses to confirm C2 connectivity. Triage question: is this malware/attacker connectivity-checking, or normal admin/troubleshooting?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Malware often verifies internet access before beaconing; a new connectivity check from an unusual host/process can be an early infection sign.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security + Sysmon + PowerShell logs via Elastic Agent (verified live). Sysmon event.code 1=process(command_line/parent populated), 11=file, 13/12=registry(registry.path populated); process.code_signature NOT collected.

Signal.Name: Internet capability check
Signal.Details: ping/tracert/pathping to a non-local target, first-seen entity.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the evidence story, not any single fact - see ClassificationGuidance.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the connectivity check is malware/attacker reconnaissance or benign troubleshooting.

Step.name: What was pinged and by which parent process
Step.Purpose: The target and the parent process separate human troubleshooting from malware connectivity checks.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-*,logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code IN ("1","4688") AND host.name == "$hostname" AND process.name RLIKE "(?i)(ping|tracert|pathping).*" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | KEEP @timestamp, process.name, process.parent.name, process.command_line, user.name | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: ping 8.8.8.8 spawned by an office app / script interpreter / unknown binary = malware connectivity check. ping by cmd.exe run by an admin = troubleshooting. The target (public DNS, C2-like domain) and parent are the discriminators.

Step.name: Process origin and account on the host
Step.Purpose: The parent process and account reveal whether this was interactive attacker activity or an automated/service context.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-*,logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code IN ("1","4688") AND host.name == "$hostname" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 2 hours | STATS runs = COUNT(*), parents = VALUES(process.parent.name), users = VALUES(user.name) BY process.name | SORT runs DESC | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: A suspicious process spawned by an office app/browser/script interpreter, run by a normal user, is more concerning than one under a known admin/automation parent.

Node.Condition: Connectivity check spawned by a suspicious parent (office app, script, dropper) or preceding C2-like connections.
Node.Result: True Positive (Malware Connectivity Check - investigate the host)

Node.Condition: Ping/tracert run by an admin or IT tool for troubleshooting.
New connectivity check with unclear parent/intent.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-NETCHK-DETAIL, INV-02-PROC-TREE to the case.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm; close as benign_activity; new_terms learns the entity.
Investigate the parent process/host; open IR if malware indicators.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A monitoring tool running connectivity checks.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm the activity on the host; if malicious indicators, isolate the host.
Identify the responsible account/process and its origin.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate the host; capture volatile evidence; hunt the same pattern across the estate.
Reset credentials used on the host if compromise is confirmed.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Remediate the root cause; add/verify EDR coverage; apply relevant hardening.

QualityChecks.Check: Confirm the required telemetry (Sysmon/Security auditing) is present on the host.
Tune known-benign administrative sources via exceptions, not by disabling the rule.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Host contained and triaged; root cause eradicated; estate swept; findings recorded.
